## Summary

Chest <u>x-ray</u> (CXR) is one of the most commonly performed imaging studies in clinical practice. CXR is a quick, noninvasive, and relatively low-radiation method to evaluate conditions and monitor procedures related to the <u>heart</u> and main vessels, <u>lungs</u>, <u>airways</u>, bones, and <u>soft tissues</u> of the thorax. Verification of patient and study data, view, and technical quality is essential before interpreting a CXR. Radiological interpretation should be performed using a systematic approach (e.g., the ABCDEFGHI mnemonic) to minimize errors while also integrating clinical findings to formulate a diagnostic impression.




General information on <u>x-ray</u> technology is found in “<u>Radiography</u>.”
